title: Share your workflow
author: Humble-Act444
selftext:
Hi Guys

Im curious to know what workflow works best for you and

which tools are you using to create games with ai. 

Models

MCP Servers

Useful websites (assets etc)

Engines

Please share 🙏

comments.author: Aromatic-Low-4578
comments.body: I'm mostly making web games. Can't recommend [https://impeccable.style/](https://impeccable.style/) enough for any sort of web design. Total gamechanger both in terms of design and accessibility.

replies.author: horatiohay
replies.body: Thanks for recommending this.  Do you have links to any of your creations?

replies.author: Aromatic-Low-4578
replies.body:
https://nervejack.gg  is my current focus. 

I'm a web dev by trade but mostly a backend guy, anything that looks nice is due to impeccable's influence.

replies.author: horatiohay
replies.body: Yeah, I'm in the same business with the same trouble 😵‍💫. Nervejack looks cool!

comments.author: Den_er_da_hvid
comments.body:
Building with löve2d in Antigravity.
I have a "component" approach, trying to keep each file under 500lines so Gemini doesn't have to read to much  each time. 

I haven't decided on art yet. As stand in I have used chatgpt and gemini and tweak in Krita.

comments.author: EpicOfBrave
comments.body:
We have custom AI agents for geometry reduction of the 3d models of the weapons and armors for our heroes.

This reduced the asset sizes a lot.

Currently working on similar approach for particle systems.

comments.author: SaltAddictedMan
comments.body:
Claude code in VS code for web apps and website.

Claude code in VS code with godot mcp server to make a game in godot

I use perplexity to help me plan and learning all this crap

comments.author: Trashy_io
comments.body: VS code co-pilot + custom built tools for myself and agents

comments.author: AgenticGameDev
comments.body:
I use AI TDD! Unit test all code (using normal Nunit) then Play mode test for all modules around 95% coverage. Then E2E tests actually having the Test play my experience. It's super hard to make it work for VR multiplayer but it's doable after a  lot of work... But the payback... Oh my. After adding new stuff and running the test and see something blow up and ask AI "/team creat an extended team and fix the MyTestMethodThatDidBreak also add in a Play mode tester to the team" and after 10 min it's fixed and I get a report. Mind blown...!   
  
However som times it get stuck and I revert back to AI with human and use the AI as a research/log tool and I do normal breakpoint debugging.

comments.author: MakkoMakkerton
comments.body:
I use GLM 5 for coding and Veo for animations 

Build structure of game first (first 5 min playable experience) If I like i add more to it. Then I add assets. Once I like how it all looks I get back to adding more features.

Consistent saves to github for safety

comments.author: ImAvoidingABan
comments.body: UE5, Rider + Claude Code, Perforce, a custom AI plugin for model and mesh generation, a custom agent for model optimization

comments.author: Classic-Ninja-1
comments.body: my workflow is simple Claude Code for coding, ChatGPT for brainstorming, and Traycer to break features into steps and planning. I build one system at a time in Unity and test as I go.
